newsitem.title: UK: UK wool sale sees mixed results.
newsitem.headline: UK wool sale sees mixed results.

text.p: The ninth sale of the season saw mixed results for UK wool, keeping the price indicator steady at 105 pence sterling per kg since the last sale on 9 October, market sources said.
Mashams sold in buyers' favour and Picks and Supers were firm while values for Halfbreds were unchanged, they said.
Prices for Welsh types fell two and a half percent and Swaledales lost between two and five pence, Marketing Board figures showed.
Crosses and Radnors were generally firm.
Forward wool made up thirty-seven percent of the total 2,611,609 kg offering and all was sold, frequently at a high premium, brokers said.
Increased competition helped to lift the overall clearance rate for the sale to 88 percent.

Some market sources said the mixed results were an indication that trading activity was beginning to get a little "There has definitely been an atmosphere of confidence building up in the auction room in recent weeks - I think we may be just seeing a tentative return of the feelgood factor for wool," one merchant said.
